fields.Participants: Marketing Manager, Visual Merchandiser, Store Manager
fields.Trigger: Annual media inventory audit; quarterly refresh

workflows.name: Retail Media Inventory Audit & Availability Mapping

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "Marketing Manager catalogs all advertising inventory" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Quantify total media inventory" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "update availability based on store remodels, new digital signage installations,…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inventory accuracy**: Media placements may be physically removed or relocated by store staff without marketing knowledge; quarterly physical verification needed
System Touchpoints: - Media inventory catalog in marketing module (W1998.1)
- Availability tracking per placement per store (W1998.2)
- Integration with W86 (planogram) for endcap and display placement mapping

steps.activity: Marketing Manager catalogs all advertising inventory: (a) in-store: (i) endcap displays (4–8 per store), (ii) power aisle promotional bays (2–4 per store), (iii) shelf talkers and wobblers (unlimited, per SKU), (iv) checkout area posters (3 per store, near POS), (v) digital screens (if installed, 1–2 per store), (vi) floor graphics (2–4 per store), (vii) shopping cart ads (if applicable), (b) ecommerce: (i) sponsored product slots (top 3 search results per category), (ii) homepage banner (1–3 slots), (iii) category page banner (1 per department × 13 departments), (iv) product page recommendation carousel, (c) print: (i) catalog back cover, inside covers, full pages, half pages, (ii) flyer inserts

Quantify total media inventory: (a) in-store: 200 stores × average 15 placements = ~3,000 in-store placements, (b) ecommerce: ~50 digital ad positions, (c) print: ~20–30 catalog positions (6 catalogs/year)
Quarterly: update availability based on store remodels, new digital signage installations, and ecommerce platform changes

fields.Frequency: Annual review; per new media type
fields.Participants: CMO, Pricing Analyst, CFO, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Annual rate card review; new media type launch

workflows.name: Retail Media Rate Card Development & Pricing Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "Pricing Analyst develops rate card" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews media pricing for margin impact" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-385 (ensure controlled execution — Retail Media Platform & Inventory Management (PA-48.1).)
- operational: CMO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rate justification**: Vendors may question media rates; BuildRight must demonstrate ROI with sales lift data from past campaigns
System Touchpoints: - Rate card management in marketing module (W1999.1)
- Pricing governance with CFO approval (W1999.2)
- Integration with W40 (price management) for rate governance

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst develops rate card: (a) in-store: (i) endcap: PHP 50K–200K/month per store (varies by location tier), (ii) shelf talker: PHP 5K–15K/month per SKU per store, (iii) checkout poster: PHP 30K–80K/month per store, (iv) digital screen: PHP 20K–50K/month per store, (b) ecommerce: (i) sponsored product: CPC (cost per click) PHP 5–20 per click, (ii) homepage banner: PHP 100K–300K/month, (iii) category banner: PHP 30K–80K/month, (c) print: (i) catalog back cover: PHP 500K–1M per edition, (ii) full page: PHP 150K–300K per edition

CFO reviews media pricing for margin impact: (a) media revenue is incremental (doesn't reduce merchandise margin), (b) ensure media pricing is competitive vs. alternative advertising channels (Facebook, Google, radio), (c) target: media revenue at 30–50% gross margin after production and placement costs
Annual: CMO benchmarks media rates against Philippine retail media market and digital advertising market; adjust rates upward as BuildRight's traffic and sales data become more valuable to vendors

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "print per store count" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-send of "sends installation photo to Visual Merchandiser for confirmation" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-validate of "checks installation compliance via store photos" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Installation non-compliance**: Store staff may not install materials promptly or correctly; photo verification and compliance scoring per store needed
System Touchpoints: - Placement order management with creative workflow (W2000.1)
- Distribution tracking via DC logistics (W2000.3)
- Photo verification of installation (W2000.3)
- Integration with W262 (store promotional setup) for physical execution
Time Estimate: - 3–5 days per campaign setup; ongoing maintenance

steps.activity: Visual Merchandiser receives placement order: (a) vendor, product, placement type, store list, duration, (b) creative assets: vendor provides artwork per BuildRight specifications (size, format, resolution, brand guidelines compliance), (c) if no creative: BuildRight in-house creative produces per vendor brief (additional fee)

Production: (a) shelf talkers/wobblers: print per store count, (b) posters: print per format and store count, (c) endcap displays: coordinate with store for product placement and signage, (d) digital screen content: upload to content management system

Distribution and installation: (a) ship printed materials to stores via DC replenishment, (b) Store Manager assigns Stock Associate for installation, (c) installation timeline: within 3 business days of receiving materials, (d) photo verification: Store Manager sends installation photo to Visual Merchandiser for confirmation

Maintenance: (a) weekly: Visual Merchandiser checks installation compliance via store photos, (b) damaged or missing materials: reorder and re-ship, (c) campaign end: Store Manager removes materials within 3 business days of campaign end date

fields.Participants: Digital Marketing Manager, Ecommerce Manager, Vendor

workflows.name: Ecommerce Sponsored Product & Banner Ad Position Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-test of "Banner ad setup" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitoring" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-385 (ensure controlled execution — Retail Media Platform & Inventory Management (PA-48.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ad relevance**: Poorly targeted ads (irrelevant products shown to wrong customers) waste vendor budget and annoy customers; continuous optimization needed
System Touchpoints: - Ecommerce advertising platform (self-service or managed) (W2001.1)
- Campaign analytics dashboard (W2001.3)
- Integration with W50 (PIM) for product data in ads

steps.activity: Digital Marketing Manager sets up sponsored product campaign: (a) vendor selects SKUs to sponsor, (b) targeting: category, search keywords, customer segments, (c) bidding: CPC model — vendor sets maximum CPC bid, (d) budget: daily or monthly cap, (e) ad creative: product image + promotional copy + price display

Banner ad setup: (a) vendor provides banner creative per specifications (size, format), (b) placement: homepage, category page, or product page, (c) targeting: all visitors, segment-based, or retargeting, (d) duration: campaign start/end dates, (e) A/B testing: 2 banner variants tested simultaneously

Campaign monitoring: (a) daily: impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, spend, (b) weekly: ROAS (return on ad spend) — vendor's sales lift attributed to advertising, (c) monthly: campaign performance report shared with vendor

fields.Trigger: Vendor or Account Manager books media placement

workflows.name: Retail Media Booking & Reservation System Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Account Manager creates booking" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "generates booking confirmation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-identify of "identify unbooked inventory for promotional pricing or internal use" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-385 (ensure controlled execution — Retail Media Platform & Inventory Management (PA-48.1).)
- operational: Marketing Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Underutilization**: ~30–40% of media inventory may go unsold; offer promotional rates to fill inventory or use for BuildRight's own marketing
System Touchpoints: - Media booking system with availability calendar (W2002.1)
- Automated booking confirmation (W2002.2)
- Integration with W13 (promotional calendar) for coordination

steps.activity: Account Manager creates booking: (a) select media type and specific placement, (b) select store list (all 200, regional, specific stores), (c) select duration (1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, per catalog edition), (d) system checks availability: is placement already booked for requested period?, (e) if available: reserve placement, (f) if unavailable: offer alternatives (different store, different dates, different placement type)

Booking confirmation: (a) system generates booking confirmation with: placement details, rate, duration, total cost, creative submission deadline, installation timeline, (b) send to vendor for approval, (c) vendor approves (or requests changes), (d) booking locked — placement reserved

Booking calendar management: (a) monthly view of all placements by store and media type, (b) identify unbooked inventory for promotional pricing or internal use, (c) overbooking prevention: system blocks double-booking of same placement

fields.Volume: ~200–400 digital screens across 200 stores (1–2 per store)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews content for brand compliance and appropriateness" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-schedule of "schedule" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "check that contracted content is playing as scheduled" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-385 (ensure controlled execution — Retail Media Platform & Inventory Management (PA-48.1).)
- operational: Digital Marketing Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Screen downtime**: Digital screens may malfunction; BuildRight must credit vendor for downtime on paid placements
System Touchpoints: - Digital signage CMS (W2003.1)
- Screen uptime monitoring (W2003.3)
- Integration with W48 (helpdesk) for screen maintenance
Time Estimate: - 30–45 min per content upload and schedule

steps.activity: Content upload: (a) vendor provides video or static creative per specifications (format: MP4/JPG, resolution: 1920×1080, duration: 15–30 sec for video), (b) Digital Marketing Manager reviews content for brand compliance and appropriateness, (c) approved content uploaded to content management system (CMS)

Scheduling: (a) assign content to specific screens (all stores, regional, specific stores), (b) set playlist: rotate vendor content with BuildRight content, (c) schedule: start/end date/time, frequency per hour, (d) priority levels: paid vendor content gets minimum guaranteed impressions

Monitoring: (a) daily: CMS reports screen uptime and content playback, (b) offline screens: IT ticket for repair per W48, (c) content compliance: periodic spot-check that contracted content is playing as scheduled

steps.activity: Portal features: (a) media catalog: browse available placements with photos and descriptions, (b) rate card: view pricing per media type and store tier, (c) availability calendar: check real-time availability, (d) booking: self-service booking with automated confirmation, (e) creative upload: submit ad creative for review, (f) campaign analytics: view performance metrics for active campaigns

Portal maintenance: (a) monthly: update availability and rate card, (b) quarterly: feature enhancements based on vendor feedback, (c) annual: platform upgrade and security review

fields.Participants: Marketing Manager, Category Manager, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Two competing vendors book adjacent or overlapping placements

workflows.name: Retail Media Conflict Resolution & Competitive Separation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "System detects competitive conflict" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "Marketing Manager resolves conflict" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-385 (ensure controlled execution — Retail Media Platform & Inventory Management (PA-48.1).)
- operational: Marketing Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor pressure**: Major vendors may demand exclusive placements; balance revenue maximization with vendor relationship management
System Touchpoints: - Automated competitive conflict detection (W2005.1)
- Booking system separation rules (W2005.2)
- Integration with W252 (item master) for competitor classification
Time Estimate: - 30–60 min per conflict; 1 day/year policy review

steps.activity: System detects competitive conflict: (a) two vendors in same product category (e.g., two paint brands) booked endcaps in same store during same period, (b) two competing appliance brands booked homepage banner in same week, (c) system flags conflict for Marketing Manager review

Marketing Manager resolves conflict: (a) competitive separation policy: competing brands should not be placed adjacent or in same visual zone during same period, (b) options: (i) offer different dates to one vendor, (ii) offer different stores (geographic separation), (iii) offer different placement types within same store (different departments), (c) if both vendors insist on same placement: first-booked priority, or highest-bid priority for contested placements

Annual: review competitive separation policy with VP Merchandising: (a) is policy too restrictive (leaving revenue on table)?, (b) is policy too lenient (creating vendor dissatisfaction)?, (c) adjust based on vendor feedback and revenue impact
